releases.title: CRTC launches new database to make it easier to identify Canadian music
releases.body:
GATINEAU, QC, Oct. 29, 2026 /CNW/ -- The CRTC is launching a free, downloadable music database that makes it easier for broadcasters, artists and the public to identify Canadian music.

For the first time, information that broadcasters use to identify Canadian music is available in one place. The database brings together information previously spread across several industry sources, making it easier for Canadian artists to be discovered and played across the country.

This will also help radio stations identify and promote music that counts toward their Canadian content requirements.

The initial release includes a large selection of popular Canadian songs. New releases and older songs will be added regularly to the database including additional French, Indigenous, and third-language music. As part of the initial phase, the CRTC welcomes feedback from users to help improve the database and ensure it continues to meet the needs of broadcasters, artists, and the public.

Quick facts

  • The CRTC is an independent quasi-judicial tribunal that regulates the Canadian communications sector in the public interest. The CRTC holds public consultations on telecommunications and broadcasting matters and makes decisions based on the public record.
  • The CRTC's new database modernizes how Canadian content is identified, making it easier and faster for broadcasters to find and play Canadian music.
  • The CRTC is continuing to provide tools, reduce administrative burden, and modernize the broadcasting framework for radio stations. This includes the CRTC recently removing the requirement for radio stations to renew their licences every few years.

STONY BROOK, N.Y., Oct. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Following Starlink's announced entry into the mobile communications space, Haloid's consulting team polled government and business land mobile radio (LMR) administrators on whether Starlink could replace, or complement, their LMR systems. We found that most radio administrators were receptive to the nascent technology but did not see it as a replacement for their LMR networks.

Sixty-seven percent of radio administrators said they would be willing to integrate Starlink technology if it allowed them to expand coverage or lower infrastructure costs. When asked whether Starlink could completely replace their LMR networks, fewer than 15 percent said yes; the vast majority believed Starlink is not as reliable as the custom networks they have built. Among administrators who already use two-way radio over cellular (also known as push-to-talk over cellular, or PoC), however, nearly 80 percent said that Starlink's satellite coverage, combined with its newly acquired cellular spectrum, would make it more desirable than the industry's wireless incumbents because it could eliminate dead spots where cellular does not reach.
releases.title: Haloid Poll: Majority of Public Safety and Commercial Radio Administrators Would Consider Starlink Integration With LMR Two-Way Radio Networks, but Disruption Unlikely
releases.body:
STONY BROOK, N.Y., Oct. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Following Starlink's announced entry into the mobile communications space, Haloid's consulting team polled government and business land mobile radio (LMR) administrators on whether Starlink could replace, or complement, their LMR systems. We found that most radio administrators were receptive to the nascent technology but did not see it as a replacement for their LMR networks.

Sixty-seven percent of radio administrators said they would be willing to integrate Starlink technology if it allowed them to expand coverage or lower infrastructure costs. When asked whether Starlink could completely replace their LMR networks, fewer than 15 percent said yes; the vast majority believed Starlink is not as reliable as the custom networks they have built. Among administrators who already use two-way radio over cellular (also known as push-to-talk over cellular, or PoC), however, nearly 80 percent said that Starlink's satellite coverage, combined with its newly acquired cellular spectrum, would make it more desirable than the industry's wireless incumbents because it could eliminate dead spots where cellular does not reach.

In the U.S., hundreds of thousands of radio users rely on traditional cellular carriers for push-to-talk communications, and that number grows each year. While the migration to two-way radio over cellular has affected the LMR industry, it has not replaced it. Many public safety agencies never made the switch, citing the risk that cellular networks could go down during weather events, power outages, or cyberattacks and jeopardize emergency communications.

In fact, during recent cellular outages, Starlink was used to provide emergency communications to affected areas, because its satellite connectivity does not depend on cell towers. But Starlink's integration with the 800 MHz cellular spectrum — "Starlink 2.0," as some experts are calling it — exposes it to some of the same vulnerabilities as traditional wireless carriers.

While Starlink's satellite service might still function if local cell towers go down, a critical portion of an agency's communications might rely on local towers using the 800 MHz spectrum, leaving the agency vulnerable in a storm or outage.

Expect evolution, not disruption

"Just like cellular didn't replace LMR, we don't see Starlink as an existential risk," said Jeremy Alicandri, President of Haloid Solutions. He expects Starlink to accelerate the industry's evolution toward shared communications infrastructure, also known as hybrid LMR. "We have public safety customers already using Starlink in their vehicles to extend the coverage of their radios. This trend will continue as Starlink devices become more ubiquitous."

The stock prices of Verizon, T-Mobile, and AT&T were affected by Starlink's recent announcement. LMR stocks such as L3Harris, JVCKENWOOD, and BK Technologies, maker of the Bendix King brand, have been unaffected, as Wall Street views Starlink as unlikely to replace LMR technology for the same reasons cellular did not. "But it may be too early to predict the industry's winners and losers," Alicandri added. "The cellular incumbents have many advantages, including low-cost devices, existing infrastructure, and their own satellite ambitions."

About Haloid Solutions Research

Haloid's Starlink poll drew on respondents to its LMR brand loyalty study, which measures radio administrators' sentiment toward the ownership and after-sales experience. Haloid's LMR research is sponsored by investors in the mission-critical communications space.

releases.title: Canadians can't control the commute, but they can control how it feels: new SiriusXM study reveals the changing experience on the road
releases.body:
Commuting experiences vary across six Canadian markets, while 73% say time on the road would be worse without audio

TORONTO, Oct. 20, 2026 /CNW/ -- For the second year in a row, SiriusXM surveyed drivers across the country to understand how their experiences are changing on the road, the regional realities shaping their journeys and the role audio plays along the way.

More than one third (37%) of Canadians say their time on the road has worsened over the past year. At the same time, as work schedules and daily routines continue to shift, changing when, why and how often Canadians are on the road, people are finding ways to make more of that time. Nearly half (47%) say their drive feels like time entirely their own, while 73% say their drive would be worse without audio.

"Canadians can't always control the traffic, distance or delays that come with being on the road, but they are able to manage how they spend that time," said Susan Simpson, Senior Director, Brand, Marketing and Communications, SiriusXM Canada. "This year's study shows the important role audio can play in that experience, and how it can help make time behind the wheel feel more enjoyable, meaningful and their own -- something SiriusXM is proud to deliver to drivers every day."

Where You Live Shapes How You Commute

The study reveals distinct commuting realities across Canadian cities:

  • Toronto drivers face some of the longest and most stressful journeys, with 27% driving for an hour or more and 48% describing the experience as stressful.
  • Vancouver drivers show that shorter drives don't always mean easier ones, with only 11% driving for an hour or more, yet 46% describing their commute as stressful.
  • Montreal drivers have a strong connection to audio, with 85% saying their time in the car would be worse without it and 31% saying audio is the part of their drive they value most.
  • Calgary commuters are most frustrated by other drivers, with 42% citing them as their top stressor, while more than half (54%) say their drive feels entirely their own.
  • Winnipeg commuters are feeling the impact of construction, with 23% citing road construction or closures as their top stressor.
  • Regina commuters report some of the most manageable journeys, with 57% travelling less than 30 minutes and 26% describing their drive as stressful.

SiriusXM has teamed up with Canadian recruiter and career expert Emily Durham (@emily.the.recruiter), whose work gives her a firsthand view into how workplace trends, hybrid schedules and changing routines are reshaping when, why and how Canadians commute.

"The way we work has changed, and so has the way we commute," said Emily Durham. "Being in the car isn't just about getting to and from the office anymore. Whether you're heading into work, dropping off the kids, going to an appointment or running errands, it can be a chance to reset and make that time feel like your own. Having something you genuinely enjoy listening to can completely change how that journey feels."

Audio Makes the Journey Better

The SiriusXM Canadian Commute study shows that audio continues to play an important role, particularly among younger Canadians. Among audio listeners aged 18–34, half (50%) say audio improves their mood, while nearly a third (32%) have looked forward to their drive because of something they planned to listen to.

SiriusXM gives Canadians the freedom to choose what they want from their drive, whether that's music to energize, news to stay informed, comedy to lighten the mood or something to help them unwind. With 425+ channels across talk, comedy, news, sports and more, plus ad free music, SiriusXM offers something for every drive, mood and moment.

Eligible customers can get SiriusXM in their car + app for $6/month for 12 months. Click here to sign up and experience what SiriusXM has to offer. See Offer Details.

Survey Methodology: These are the findings of a survey conducted by Angus Reid Group on behalf of SiriusXM from September 1-9, 2026 among a sample of n=1,256 working adults living in Canada who commute by car and are members of the Angus Reid Forum. The survey was conducted in English and French. For comparison purposes only, a probability sample of this size would carry a margin of error of ±2.8 percentage points, 19 times out of 20.

releases.body:
SiriusXM offers live broadcasts of every game from Opening Night through NBA Finals

Daily NBA talk and analysis airs 365 days a year on the exclusive SiriusXM NBA Radio channel, hosted by former players, executives and other league experts

TORONTO, Oct. 19, 2026 /CNW/ -- SiriusXM will deliver fans across North America the most comprehensive audio coverage of the NBA, offering live broadcasts of every NBA game from Opening Night through the NBA postseason and The Finals, as well as daily NBA talk programming every day of the year on the exclusive SiriusXM NBA Radio channel.

The 2026-27 NBA season begins with a star-studded tripleheader tomorrow, October 20. At 3:00 pm ET Jayson Tatum and the Boston Celtics visit the Detroit Pistons and one of the league's brightest young stars, Cade Cunningham, at Little Caesars Arena. At 7:00 pm ET in New York's Madison Square Garden, Jalen Brunson and the reigning NBA Champion Knicks host the Philadelphia 76ers and a new-look roster that now features LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. Then at 9:30 pm ET, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the Oklahoma City Thunder travel to San Antonio to take on the reigning Western Conference Champion Spurs and the generational talent of Victor Wembanyama at the Frost Bank Center.

All three matchups will air on the SiriusXM NBA Radio channel, which is available to listeners nationwide in their cars (channel 86) and on the SiriusXM app.

Every NBA game, from the regular season through The Finals, is available to SiriusXM listeners. Those listening via the SiriusXM app, or in vehicles equipped with SiriusXM's latest generation 360L radios, get the added benefit of being able to access both the home and visiting team broadcasts for every matchup.

Throughout the year, fans can follow all the latest NBA news on the exclusive SiriusXM NBA Radio channel. The channel's daily lineup features talk shows hosted by former players, coaches, executives and other league experts, and fans can call in to be a part of the conversation each day.

releases.title: BEASLEY MEDIA GROUP NAMED OFFICIAL AUDIO PARTNER OF VEGAS GOLDEN KNIGHTS
releases.body:
NAPLES, Fla., Sept. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Beasley Media Group has been named the official year-round audio partner of the Vegas Golden Knights, launching a multiyear agreement that will deliver English- and Spanish-language game broadcasts and expanded VGK programming across Beasley's audio and digital platforms. The VGK Radio Network is presented by Lee's Discount Liquor. 

Under the agreement, X 107.9 (KVGS FM) will serve as the team's official English-language radio flagship, while 105.7 Maxima (KOAS FM) will become the Spanish-language radio home of the Golden Knights. The two-station structure will broaden access to live game coverage while serving the diverse audiences that follow the team throughout Southern Nevada.

Dan D'Uva and Gary Lawless will return for their 10th season as the Golden Knights' official English-language radio broadcast team, with D'Uva handling play-by-play and Lawless providing analysis. X 107.9 will broadcast all of Vegas' games during the 2026-27 season with D'Uva and Lawless. Doug Lattuca will serve as host of the broadcasts on X 107.9, providing live coverage from every pregame, postgame, and intermission. Jesus Lopez and Alex Romo will also return to the Golden Knights and Beasley Media Group team as the Spanish-language play-by-play voice on 105.7 Maxima (KOAS-FM). 

The VGK Insider Show will return with Daren Millard as host of the hour-long program on X 107.9. The show will air each weekday from 5 to 6 p.m. PT and feature consistent appearances from Kelly McCrimmon, the General Manager of the Golden Knights, as well as players and broadcasters from the team and other personalities around the NHL. The VGK Insider Show will make its debut for the season on Monday, Sept. 28 on X 107.9.

The Henderson Silver Knights will broadcast on X 107.9 and 96.3 KKLZ-HD2 with full pregame and postgame coverage, carrying all 72 regular-season games and the Calder Cup Playoffs. Brian McCormack will provide play-by-play and Darren Eliot will serve as color analyst as the Silver Knights celebrate their seventh American Hockey League season.

"We're excited to partner with Beasley Media Group as we continue to advance our brand and connect with more fans throughout Las Vegas and Southern Nevada. With 107.9 X as our flagship station and 105.7 Maxima serving as our Spanish-language home, we'll be able to reach fans across the region through our radio broadcasts," said John Penhollow, President of Business Operations for the Vegas Golden Knights. "This partnership gives us a great opportunity to connect with our fans in new and meaningful ways throughout the year, not just on game days, and will broaden the connection to the Golden Knights and the future stars with the Silver Knights."

"Las Vegas is the sports and entertainment capital of the world, and the Golden Knights are the team that made it so. Beasley's four Las Vegas stations reach every corner of this valley, and now every one of them carries the team — with X 107.9 as the home of the Golden Knights and Máxima as their Spanish-language home," said Kevin LeGrett, chief business officer at Beasley Media Group.

The agreement expands Beasley's presence in live sports and creates an integrated platform for Golden Knights programming across broadcast radio, digital audio, podcasts and other content channels. It also provides the team and its partners with year-round opportunities to reach fans in Las Vegas and throughout the Golden Knights' radio affiliate network.

ABOUT THE VEGAS GOLDEN KNIGHTS

The Vegas Golden Knights are a National Hockey League franchise owned and operated by Black Knight Sports and Entertainment LLC. Established by Owner and Chairman Bill Foley and his family, the Golden Knights were the most successful expansion franchise in North American professional sports history in 2017-18 and won the Stanley Cup in 2022-23. The Golden Knights have advanced to the Stanley Cup Final three times and celebrate their 10th season as a franchise in 2026-27. For the latest news and information on the Golden Knights visit vegasgoldenknights.com and follow the team on Facebook, X, Instagram and TikTok.

ABOUT THE HENDERSON SILVER KNIGHTS

The Henderson Silver Knights are the American Hockey League affiliate of the Vegas Golden Knights. The Silver Knights are owned in part by Bill Foley and his family and operated by the Foley Entertainment Group. The Silver Knights play their home games at Lee's Family Forum, a state-of-the-art arena in Henderson, NV. For the latest news and information on the Silver Knights visit hendersonsilverknights.com and follow the team on Facebook, X and Instagram.

ABOUT BEASLEY MEDIA GROUP

Beasley Media Group LLC is a multiplatform media company providing advertising and digital marketing solutions across the United States. The company owns and operates radio properties located in 49 large and mid-size markets across the country and offers capabilities in audio technology, podcasting, e-commerce and events. Beasley Media Group reaches over 20 million consumers weekly through on-air, online and digital platforms.

releases.body:
The competition celebrates eight years in partnership with the CCMA at Country Music Week, delivering a $25,000 grand prize and $10,000 awarded to each runner-up

TORONTO, Sept. 17, 2026 /CNW/ -- Following last night's live finale in Saskatoon, SiriusXM Canada, in partnership with the Canadian Country Music Association® (CCMA®), announced Blue Ridge Band as the winner of the 2026 SiriusXM Top of the Country competition. Fellow finalists Shawnee Kish and Morgan Griffiths were named runners-up, closing out an exciting year of mentorship opportunities and live performances.

The finale was broadcast live on SiriusXM's Top of the Country Radio (Ch. 155), giving country music fans across Canada the chance to tune in, vote live and share in the excitement as the 2026 competition came to a close.

Taking the stage one final time, all three finalists delivered standout performances in front of a live audience and a panel of industry experts and judges. After months of competition, Shawnee Kish, Morgan Griffiths and Blue Ridge Band showcased their unique sounds and styles, with Blue Ridge Band ultimately securing the 2026 title and $25,000 grand prize. Runners-up Shawnee Kish and Morgan Griffiths each received $10,000. The celebration was followed by a headline performance from Jade Eagleson with special guest SACHA.

"This competition has definitely been one for the books," said the Blue Ridge Band. "Being part of this program and competing alongside such talented Canadian artists has been a highlight of my career so far. I'm incredibly grateful to SiriusXM and the CCMA for their support throughout this experience, and I'm so excited for what comes next."

The road to the 2026 SiriusXM Top of the Country finale began earlier this year, when country artists from across Canada put their names forward for a chance to take the national stage. Eight semi-finalists were selected to record original songs and videos before fans voted to determine the final three. Along the way, the top three finalists gained valuable experience through mentorship from leading voices in country music and live performances at major events, including CMA Fest in Nashville and LASSO Montréal.

"This year's finalists are a testament to the depth of country talent across Canada," said Michelle Mearns, Senior Vice President of Programming and Operations at SiriusXM Canada. "It's been rewarding to watch them grow throughout the competition, and we're incredibly proud to continue amplifying Canadian talent. Congratulations to the Blue Ridge Band on a well-deserved win."

"The CCMA's partnership with SiriusXM Canada has helped educate, elevate and celebrate emerging artists across the Canadian country music community," said Amy Jeninga, President, CCMA. "Seeing these artists bring their passion and creativity to every stage of the competition, and knowing the program is creating meaningful opportunities for the next steps in their careers, is what makes Top of the Country so special. We're incredibly proud to celebrate another great year."

SiriusXM Top of the Country, in partnership with the CCMA, is part of SiriusXM's ongoing tradition of promoting and elevating the best emerging Canadian music talent. SiriusXM continues to offer a leading platform for Canadian artists through its significant financial contributions and North American-wide reach.

releases.title: SiriusXM's SXM-11 Satellite Successfully Completes In-Orbit Testing and Enters Operational Service
releases.body:
Most powerful satellite in SiriusXM's fleet is designed to improve signal reception, expand Alaska coverage and support reliable service across North America

NEW YORK, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SiriusXM today announced that the Company's SXM-11 satellite is now operational, following successful in-orbit testing and handover by Intuitive Machines. SXM-11 is the most powerful satellite in SiriusXM's high-powered fleet and is designed to improve signal reception, expand Alaska coverage and support reliable service across North America.

"Bringing SXM-11 into service strengthens our next-generation satellite fleet and reinforces the long-term resilience of our network," said Sean Gibbons, Chief Product and Technology Officer at SiriusXM. "For listeners, that means a premium in-car experience with broad, reliable coverage, including where cellular service may be limited. Through SiriusXM with 360L, we combine that reach with the choice, personalization and interactivity of streaming, to bring the best of both technologies together in millions of vehicles."

210 million SiriusXM-equipped vehicles across North America are on the road today and rely on the proprietary satellite infrastructure supporting SiriusXM's in-vehicle listening experience. Built on the Intuitive Machines IM 1300™ satellite platform, SXM-11 weighed more than 15,000 pounds, or nearly 6,950 kilograms at launch. The satellite stands 28 feet tall and spans more than 106 feet with its solar panels deployed. Orbiting 22,000 miles above Earth, SXM-11 features a large, unfurlable 30-foot (9 meter) main beam antenna that broadcasts audio and data to users on the ground, with an estimated eight million square miles of broadcast coverage.

"SXM-11 marks another milestone in our longstanding partnership with SiriusXM. Over the course of our relationship, we have built 13 spacecraft together," said Chris Johnson, President, Intuitive Machines. "This handover reflects our shared commitment to mission success and the confidence SiriusXM continues to place in our team to deliver high-performance, reliable space systems. We continue to demonstrate our ability to design, build, and deliver satellite systems that meet the demanding requirements of today's commercial space market with robust, scalable high-power platforms."

SiriusXM also offers satellite-delivered Marine and Aviation services that provide pilots and boaters with weather data and other important information directly in their cockpits. SXM-11 carries an additional communications payload that will be used to deliver expanded WCS-band coverage.

SXM-11 launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station at 10:25 p.m. ET on June 28. SiriusXM and Intuitive Machines subsequently completed the commissioning and testing required to verify that the spacecraft and its communications systems were ready for operational service.

SXM-11 is the 15th satellite launched for SiriusXM and will replace XM-5. It is part of SiriusXM's ongoing satellite fleet-refresh program. SXM-9 and SXM-10 commenced service in 2025, and SXM-12 is currently scheduled for launch in 2027.

SXM-11 by the numbers

  • More than 15,000 pounds: SXM-11's launch weight, approximately the weight of a school bus.
  • Nearly 60%: The portion of the satellite's launch weight made up of fuel supporting its journey and in-orbit operations.
  • 28 feet: The height of the satellite.
  • 22,000 miles: The satellite's orbiting distance above Earth.
  • 8 million square miles: The satellite's approximate broadcast coverage footprint.
  • More than 106 feet: The satellite's span with its solar panels deployed - approximately the height of a 10-story building laid on its side.
  • 30 feet: The diameter of SXM-11's large, unfurlable S-band reflector (9 meters).
  • 210 million: The estimated number of SiriusXM-equipped vehicles across North America supported by SiriusXM's proprietary satellite network.
  • 15th satellite: SXM-11 is the 15th spacecraft launched for Sirius, XM and SiriusXM.

About Sirius XM Holdings Inc.

SiriusXM is the leading audio entertainment company in North America, with a portfolio of audio businesses including its flagship subscription entertainment service SiriusXM; the ad-supported and premium music streaming services of Pandora; an expansive podcast network; and a complete ecosystem of advertising solutions through SiriusXM Media and AdsWizz. SiriusXM offers live, on-demand, and human-curated programming across music, talk, news, sports, and podcasts, and the company reaches approximately 255 million monthly listeners across its platforms. With deep automotive manufacturer relationships and unique spectrum assets, SiriusXM is built to reach listeners wherever they are. The company connects fans to the voices, creators, and moments they love - creating communities where listeners engage, participate, and belong. For more about SiriusXM, please go to: https://www.siriusxm.com/

About Intuitive Machines

Intuitive Machines is a leading space infrastructure company that builds spacecraft, connects networks and operates infrastructure-as-a-service for commercial, civil and national-security customers. With a proven track record across the space domain, the company, through organic growth and portfolio expansion, has built more than 300 spacecraft, delivered more than 260 kilograms of payload to the lunar surface and provided precision-navigation expertise that has guided spacecraft across the solar system. These capabilities form an integrated Build-Connect-Operate infrastructure service company, enabling customers to achieve mission and campaign outcomes through a single prime solution. Intuitive Machines' technology has been demonstrated across the space domain and is engineered to support the next century of opportunity in space.
